correctness.rationale: In an unfilled graph, the descending link is the discrete set of earlier neighbors, a cone exactly when that set has one vertex. A selected pair (v,u) therefore forces u before v and v before each other neighbor. Conversely a topological order of these requirements realizes every selected pair, and any extras are harmless in the downward closure. In a forest only opposed directions on an edge can form a directed cycle. Any such conflict has a two-incidence witness: distinct choices at the same center conflict along one of its chosen edges; choices at different centers can conflict only along their common edge, either when both choose the other or neither does. Counting separately by center and by original edge yields the conflict graph and its size formula. On C_n the selected even centers comprise a minimum cover, since each selected center covers two edges and all edges are covered. Orienting each selected center from its predecessor to its successor forces the full forward cycle; removing any one selection uncovers an edge and leaves a proper forward subgraph. The resulting minimal nonface has ceil(n/2) vertices. On C_3 no pair survives: two different centers either conflict on their common edge or force the full cycle. On C_4 a pair at adjacent centers is allowed with the same orientation sign (8 pairs), and one at opposite centers with opposite signs (4 pairs). Any triple on distinct centers has a consecutive chain of three, forcing equal signs on that chain if pairwise compatible, contrary to compatibility of its opposite endpoints. So both short cycles are flag with the reported maximal faces. Independently compared 15,752 incidence subsets with downward-closed enumerations of all orders on all nonempty labeled graphs on 2–4 vertices, and explicitly counted short-cycle facets (python3 /workspace/branches/independent-replay.py 4).
residual_risks: The finite replay is not a general certificate; the general claims rest on the order and incidence proofs. The frozen output's 13 complete matchings on C_4 are not 13 facets; the frozen verification notes distinguish those counts. Triangles here are not filled simplices.

evidence: The dihedral-Euler proof's criterion covers every incidence configuration on all C_n for n>=3, thus more than a single minimal-nonface construction.

Knudson–Owens-White give the strong filtration definition and short-cycle homotopy results. Donovan–Scoville's flag result is about the ordinary Morse complex whose faces are regular gradient vector fields.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact face criterion is strong enough to entail (C), whereas homotopy equivalence alone is not. Ordinary tree flagness does not automatically pass to a non-induced strong subcomplex and does not give its additional adjacent-center conflict. The inspected cycle-specific theorem cannot be applied directly to arbitary graphs or to forest conflicts as a general algorithm.

evidence: The all-cycle test forbids differing adjacent nonzero signs; with only one nonzero sign it requires consecutive zeros. The all-zero choice is allowed.

A maximum independent set in C_n has floor(n/2) vertices and is maximal. Put zeros there and + on its complement. There are no consecutive zeros and hence no face. Deleting a + creates adjacent zeros because the independent set is maximal; now the criterion accepts. There are ceil(n/2) pluses.

For n=3 the test rules out every two-center selection. For n=4 it accepts same-sign adjacent pairs and opposite-sign opposite pairs; no triple is pairwise compatible. This also gives the claimed short-cycle onset.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The original (C) construction is exactly the complement-of-independent-set configuration in the prior test. Downward closure makes deletion of any one selected incidence sufficient for minimality; for n>=5 its size is at least three. Thus rewriting the prior signs as a directed cycle does not supply a new exact result here. Tree purity and maximum-facet statements do not give the full forest conflict graph, and the derivation does not reject (A) or (B) as already known.

evidence: The primary strong complex is the downward closure of matchings generated by vertex filtrations. Omitting the empty face changes none of the nonempty tests.

On a cycle the prior encodes each center by 0 if unmatched, + if its selected incidence forces forward orientation on both incident edges, and - for reverse orientation. Distinct selections at the same center are inherently incompatible.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The sign description and precedence arcs encode identical constraints on the same labeled, unfilled cycle. Conflicting adjacent signs make a two-cycle; without such a conflict the only remaining directed cycle is the whole cycle in one direction. Thus the prior gives the same face decision on C_n, not merely a similar homotopy invariant.

value.rationale: The general oracle reduces an enumeration over strict filtrations to explicit precedence constraints and a topological sort, and the forest model supplies a local independence graph and a closed edge count for an unbounded class. Those are useful exact structural tools. By contrast the cycle obstruction and small-cycle flag onset add no distinct scientific value beyond the covering exact cycle criterion; the value pass rests on (A) outside the prior cycle setting and (B), not on counting (C) as new.
residual_risks: The forest model does not by itself compute homotopy types; the cycle corollary is not an independent new contribution.
